texts.preamble: Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Kabc020203802019 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.4779/2019 Dated this 16th day of April, 2025 Petitioner: Arbaaz Khan S/o Aslam Khan, Aged about 20 years, No.275, 8th Cross, Gangondanahalli, Bengaluru South, Nayandahalli, Bengaluru - 560 039. (Sri R. Venkatesha Naidu, Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Nandi Glass and Plywoods, No.19/1, 1st Cross, Byatarayanapura, Mysore Road, Bengaluru - 560 026. (Rc owner of the Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462) (Sri Raviteja, Advocate) 2 Mvc No.4779/2019 2. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., T.P. Hub, Leo Shopping Complex, No.44/45, 4th Floor, Residency Road, Bengaluru - 25. (Insurer of the Tata 407 Tempo Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/ 1 bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462) (Policy No.421902/31/2019/508, valid from 09-05-2018 to 08-05-2019) (Sri Udaya Krishna, Advocate) 3. Veena A. W/o S. Amaresh,
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 24-04-2019 at about 1:00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760, from Nayandahalli Bus Stop side to R.R. Arch side, on Mysore road, near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru. At that time, the Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came at high speed from R.R. Arch side on the other side of the said road, which is bifurcated by a stone Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/ 2 median and suddenly took a right turn where there is a provision for the same to go to Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, without giving any signal to the vehicles either coming on his back side or coming in front of the said Tata 407 Tempo and without observing the vehicles plying on the other side of the said road and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner, which was also being ridden by its rider at high speed, in rash and negligent manner. In order to avoid the accident, the rider of said scooter took the same to the extreme left side of the road, due to which the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body and the said Honda Dio Scooter was also damaged. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment and thereafter he was shifted to SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie and was earning sum of Rs.22,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle and driver of the Tata 407 Tempo for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tata 407 Tempo and the respondent No.3 is the owner and respondent No.4 is the rider of the Honda Dio Scooter. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. Whereas, the respondent No.4 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.4 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him. Further, it has denied the manner of accident as narrated in the petition. It has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. Further it is contended that, the driver of its Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 was driving the vehicle slowly, carefully and cautiously, observing all traffic rules and regulations came from R.R. Arch towards Nayandahalli and when he reached near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, for the puspose of filling the diesel to the vehicle, showing the indicator, slowly taking right turn towards Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, at that time the rider of scooter along with a pillion rider, without wearing helmet and without holding valid driving licence, riding a Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760, doing wheeling on one wheel, came from Nayandahalli towards R.R. Arch in Mysore road at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules and regulations, so as to endangering human life and property, all of a sudden came and dashed against the left side door and safety guard of the battery of the respondent No.1 vehicle. The driver of its vehicle has lodged a complaint against the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 on the same day to the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police . The police have registered the case against the rider of said scooter and seized the said two-wheeler and issued notice under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, to its RC owner i.e. respondent No.3. The respondent Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/ 3 No.3 has received the said notice and given reply to the same, stating that the said two-wheeler was not having valid insurance policy and its rider was also not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident. Further it is contended that, the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have filed the charge-sheet under Section 279, 337, 338 of I.P.C., Section 189, 3(1) R/w 181, 146 R/w 196, 5 R/w 180 of Motor Vehicles Act against the rider of the Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 and all the police documents clearly demonstrate and reveal that, the said accident has occurred due to wheeling at high speed, in rash and negligent manner by the rider of said scooter and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo and he was not at all responsible for the alleged accident. It has admitted that, the respondent No.1 is the registered certificate owner of the Tata 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-05- AF-8462 and all the records relating to the said vehicle are standing in his name and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 under policy No.421902/31/2019/508 and same was valid from 09-05-2018 to 08-05-2019 and the driver of its vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.1.
texts.arguments: It has contended that, there is a negligence on the part of the petitioner himself to proceed as a pillion rider on the Honda Dio Scooter bearing No.KA-04-ED-4760 by not taking proper care and precaution, since the said petitioner was talking with the rider of the said scooter and shaking by his act, which is a clear negligence on the part of the petitioner. The rider of the Honda Dio Scooter was also negligent in riding the said scooter by not following traffic rules and regulations, as he was wheeling i.e. lifting the front wheel of the said scooter and was riding the said scooter on the back wheel, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the tempo bearing No.KA-05-AF-8462. Hence, the police have charge-sheeted the rider by name Mohammed Afreed S/o Taj Mohammed, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. and Section 189, 3(1) R/w 181, 146 R/w 196, 5 R/w 180 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is a self evidentiary to point out that the rider of the scooter was not holding driving licence to ride the said scooter and was riding the same in rash and negligent manner, at the time of accident. Further it is contended that, there is no insurance policy to the Honda Dio Scooter, both petitioner/pillion rider and rider of the said Honda Dio Scooter were not wearing helmets at the time of accident. There is negligence on the part of petitioner himself and also negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Dio Scooter. On the other hand, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AF-8462, as he was driving the said vehicle slowly, carefully and following all traffic rules and regulations. The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the insurer of the Honda Dio Scooter has not been made as party to the proceedings. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 6. Whereas, the respondent No.3 in her written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. She has contended that, the alleged Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/ 4 was sold by her on 27-08-2015 to one Rajesh M. S/o Mani, No.34, 9th Main, 3rd Cross, Srirampuram, Bengaluru - 21, for a sum of Rs.3,000/-, and after the said sale transaction, both of them have mutually agreed to transfer their responsibilities in between them by issuing the following documents to each other, which are proper and legal documents as per the Motor Vehicles Act to transfer the ownership and insurance of the said vehicle. The delivery note, sale receipt, transfer of insurance, no objection to issue clearance certificate, the original registration certificate and original policy were handed over to the purchaser. After receiving the sale consideration amount and proper documents with endorsement from the said Rajesh, the said vehicle was handed over to him on the same day and accordingly, she had lost her ownership, responsibility and obligations over the said said vehicle from 27-08-2015. Hence, the petition against her is bad for mis-joinder, as she has been unnecessarily made as party, with ulterior motive to claim compensation. Further it is contended that, she was not at all the legal registration certificate owner of the alleged Honda Dio Scooter, at the time of accident. She do not know who was riding the said scooter and also who had handed over it to the rider on 24-04-2019 to ply on road. At the time of accident, the said scooter was not in her custody and hence the rider of the scooter was not riding the same with consent of respondent No.3, as there is no relationship as the rider and owner in between them. Further she has contended that, on perusal of the entire police documents it is clear that, the driver of the Tempo 407 Light Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 has lodged the complaint before the jurisdictional police with all malafide intentions to escape from the offence punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of I.P.C., by colluding with the police and has falsely impleaded her in the present proceedings. She has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him. She has contended that, if at all the alleged accident has happened, it is only due to the careless and negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo 407 Goods vehicle and the respondent No.4/rider/subsequent purchaser of the above said Honda Dio Scooter negligence. In view of the above said facts and circumstances, she is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and if at all she is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner, it is only by the insured and insurer of the tempo 407 goods vehicle and the respondent No.4/rider/subsequent purchaser of the above said Honda Dio Scooter and not by this respondent. The learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, the Ex.P.4 sketch clearly speaks that, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 tried his level best to avoid the accident, but as the Tata 407 tempo came with high speed from R.R. Arch side and suddenly took a right turn to go to Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, without giving any signal and without observing the vehicles plying on the said road, he could not avoid the said accident and as such the said accident has taken place due to composite rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760. Hence, the owner and insurer of both the vehicles are liable to compensate the petitioner, for the injuries caused to him in the said accident. In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on the following judgments: i) Sarjito Devi and others V/s Jaswinder and others, reported in 2019 ACJ 1479. ii) United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s H.J. Rajendra and others, reported in 2015 ACJ 176. iii) Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation V/s Narendrabhai Lalbhai Shah and others, reported in 2010 ACJ 15. iv) Sudhir Kumar Rana V/s Surinder Singh and others, reported in 2008 ACJ 1834. Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/ 8 v) Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation V/s Sisir Rajendrakumar Mishra and others, reported in 2014 ACJ 2679. In such circumstances, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner does not holds good and the ratio laid down in the above cited judgments are not applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required . " 20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered physical disability and he is not in a position to perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his learning capacity. Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability. ii) Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
